newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end close to all-time high.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end close to all-time high.

text.p: French stocks closed more than one percent higher on Tuesday, setting a new high for the year, but fell short of matching their all-time high.
Traders said the bourse was lifted by a stronger dollar and growing expectations of near-term interest rate cuts in Europe.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed 30.48 points or 1.31 percent higher at 2,349.11 -- within reach of its historic record of 2,360.98 set in February 1994.
The CAC-40 futures contract ended the session at 2,352.0, up 30.5 points from its close on Monday. At 1605 GMT, the future was down at 2,349.0.
Companies with U.S. units, heavy exports toward the United States or in competition with U.S. manufacturers were big gainers during the session thanks to the dollar's surge.
The dollar was worth 1.5662 marks late on Tuesday.
The dollar gained after Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said this week that he had no objection to a higher dollar.
Chief Bundesbank Economist Otmar Issing's prediction on Monday that investors could switch assets into dollars in the early stages of European monetary union also lifted the unit.
New York Federal Reserve Bank President William McDonough echoed Issing's comments early on Tuesday.
"The dollar may take on a bit more relative importance as a reserve currency," in the run up to and in the first years after the start of a single currency, McDonough told a conference.
Dealers said the CAC-40 was likely to rise through its all time high on Wednesday, but said a durable bull run from here depended largely on the U.S. stock market.
Volume was a very heavy 8.5 billion francs with 6.3 billion on the blue chip CAC-40.
* LVMH up 4.42 percent to 1,394 francs, third-biggest gainer for the day on heavy volume, as flagship luxury goods group a chief beneficiary of dollar's rise.
*Other stocks to benefit from dollar include Elf up 1.03 percent, Total up 0.99 percent, Metaleurop up 3.53 percent and Michelin up 2.87 percent.
* Eurotunnel up 2.96 percent to 6.95 francs as stock rebounds after fall due to fire in Channel tunnel. Dealers said they expect passenger traffic to restart soon.
* Groupe Andre rises 3.99 percent as rumours persist of a possible alliance with Pinault-Printemps. Pinault down 0.72 percent.
* Credit Lyonnais loses 0.95 percent on word of investigation of former managers of the troubled state bank.

* Paribas and unit Cie Bancaire up 1.72 percent and 4.11 percent, respectively, on rumours that Bancaire, a unit of Paribas would sell a large stake of Cetelem to pay for provisioning of Sinvim's real estate exposure.
*Cetelem down 1.27 percent on the rumours.
*Bouygues fell 2.76 percent on rumours of a capital increase tied to the purchase of St. Gobain's CISE unit. St Gobain up 1.6 percent.
